title: Logical Replication & CDC
description: Publish and subscribe to table changes, replicate across different PostgreSQL versions, and power Change Data Capture (CDC).

data.text: While physical streaming replication replicates the entire cluster at the disk block level, **Logical Replication** operates on a **publish/subscribe model** for individual tables. It decodes WAL records into logical row changes (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

data.title: Configuring Publication and Subscription
data.content: Replicating specific tables across distinct databases.

data.text: Initial Sync, Conflicts, and Slot Lag

Logical replication has two phases: an initial copy of the table's existing rows, then a continuous stream of changes from the publisher's WAL. The subscriber applies changes through normal SQL, so a conflicting row — say a unique key that already exists on the subscriber — aborts that transaction and the subscription stops until you resolve it. The publisher's replication slot retains WAL until the subscriber confirms it, so a stalled subscriber will grow the publisher's disk.

data.title: Monitor the subscription and the publisher slot
data.content: Run the first query on the subscriber and the second on the publisher. A growing `retained_wal` with an inactive slot is the classic disk-fill warning.
data.code:
-- On the subscriber: replication health
SELECT subname, pid, received_lsn, latest_end_lsn,
       now() - last_msg_receipt_time AS since_last_message
FROM pg_stat_subscription;

-- On the publisher: how much WAL is being retained for this slot?
SELECT slot_name, active,
       pg_size_pretty(
           pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)
       ) AS retained_wal
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE slot_name = 'sub_app';

data.title: Logical replication is not for automatic failover
data.text: Logical replication has no concept of a primary: it copies row changes to a subscriber that can still be written to independently, and it does not replay DDL, sequence values, or large objects. Those gaps mean it cannot be promoted transparently in an outage — you would have to reconcile divergence by hand. Use logical replication for cross-version upgrades, selective replication, and Change Data Capture, and use physical streaming replication with a consensus-based failover manager when you need automatic HA.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Logical replication works across different major PostgreSQL versions (e.g. PG 14 to PG 16).
Allows replicating a subset of tables or filtering by rows.
Forms the foundation for Change Data Capture (CDC) with tools like Debezium and Kafka.
